A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the MiCRo framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material that was renamed, redrawn, or relocated.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, expert ablations, routing analyses, neuroscience-localizer experiments, and medical-domain and test-time-scaling results.

after.justification: V2 reports original model evaluations and analyses, including CogBench experiments, correlations with human ratings, architectural comparisons, and DPO experiments, alongside retained results.

M1.justification: The four-expert full-block architecture and three-stage training curriculum remain intact. V2 adds a MiCRo-MoE adaptation with FFN-only experts and shared attention (Appendix G), plus optional DPO post-training (Appendix F). These are limited extensions of the retained framework; the MoB and MiCRoSFT terminology does not itself change the method.

E1.justification: V2 adds CogBench psychological tasks, independently human-rated sentences, generated domain-specific probes, HellaSwag and ARC evaluations, and preference training data for DPO. PIQA gains evaluation coverage after already appearing in the training mixture. EWoK, ToMi, and DROP evaluations disappear. The curated expert-training mixture, core reasoning benchmarks, Empathy routing evaluation, and medical benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Dense and unspecialized full-block baseline roles persist under the Dense and MoB names. V2 adds a MoB ablation comparator in Figure 7 and a conventional FFN-only MoE comparator in Table 6. Conversely, v1's standard OLMo benchmark comparison against No Experts and General is absent from v2's corresponding benchmark results, although OLMo medical comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 expands model configurations beyond the two original 1B backbones and introduces CogBench evaluation using log-probability choices and human-normalized similarity. Localizer selection changes from the top 1% to 10% of units, and routing aggregation changes from modal expert assignments to aggregation across layers. GPT-4o-defined ablation clusters are replaced by standard MMLU categories and aggregate BBH results. Figure 7 also selects the best result after ablating up to one expert, replacing v1's intuitive benchmark-level selection.

E4.justification: V2 adds correlations between routing and human judgments, DPO robustness tests, and architectural analyses identifying failed specialization in larger MiCRo-MoE models. Expert ablations and qualitative steering examples are expanded and revised. Training-stability analysis now probes all four generated domains instead of Empathy alone. V1's analysis of varying the number of active experts at inference is removed.

E5.justification: Although v1 already displays some error bars, v2 adds explicit standard errors in benchmark tables, pairwise Welch's t-tests in Figure 7, and five random seeds for CogBench experiments. Routing captions also identify variation across samples. These substantially expand statistical reporting; the five-seed statement concerns behavioral evaluation, not repeated model training.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial behavioral, correlation, DPO, MoE, and expanded benchmark results, while removing earlier benchmark and test-time-scaling entries. Reported Llama-1B Dense GSM8K accuracy changes from 35.7 in v1 Table 1 to 36.8 in v2 Table 3, whereas MiCRo remains 34.7. New Figure 15 reports a 0.70 social-routing/mental-state correlation in middle layers. CogBench advantages vary by model scale. Medical results remain numerically unchanged between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 5.

T1.justification: V2 Section 5.4 introduces BRE_i = |s_i - 1| / max(1, s_i) and S_BRE = 1 - mean(BRE_i), together with a boundedness claim intended to handle superhuman scores. This is a limited mathematical definition absent from v1. The existing training notation is substantively unchanged, and no broader theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: V2 makes human behavioral alignment a central contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. It changes v1's broad reasoning-performance improvement claim to matching or exceeding comparable baselines while retaining interpretability. Correlation with human judgments becomes supporting evidence for the central specialization claim, and the introduction's test-time compute-scaling claim is removed.

C2.justification: V2 revises the localizer interpretation to emphasize early language-expert and later world-expert selectivity, and proposes scale-dependent emergence as an explanation for ToM localization. It adds architectural failure conditions, interprets behavioral alignment across scales, and specifies obstacles to neural validation involving suitable fMRI data. The scaling limitation moves from beyond 1B to beyond 3B base models; the earlier test-time-scaling tradeoff discussion disappears.

D1.justification: Core training hyperparameters and the detailed expert-data table are retained. V2 adds the GPT-5 stimulus-generation prompt, human-rating analysis details, and more explicit benchmark metric specifications. It removes the four-A100 hardware disclosure and v1's explicit randomized-routing baseline description, and changes the project access address. Revised sampling prose agrees more closely with the retained appendix mixture; it does not establish a changed training dataset.

R1.justification: V2 updates citations for emergent modularity, Switch Transformers, CogBench, human ratings, and DPO, while removing some earlier references such as Continuous Thought Machines and Topoformer. Section 2.2 adds an explicit first-model claim for inducing this brain-network specialization. These refine the retained positioning within modular and brain-inspired language modeling.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, results narrative, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Related work moves into the early background section, and performance evaluation follows specialization and behavioral analyses. Dataset and baseline terminology changes throughout, and the appendices are substantially reorganized. These changes exceed the prose needed merely to insert new experiments.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redesigned, and main benchmark comparisons shift from a table to Figure 7's bar charts with significance annotations. Routing, ablation, and localizer displays are rebuilt or expanded, with new behavioral and correlation figures. Medical results move to an appendix table. The unchanged pseudo-labeling prompt and examples are relocated, while the overall figure organization and document layout change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's explicit absence of behavioral validation through CogBench and independent human-rating correlations (Figures 6, 15, and 18). Architectural failure analyses, broader scale testing, and more explicit statistical reporting substantially strengthen evidence for the central specialization argument and clarify its boundaries. Some earlier benchmark coverage and hardware disclosure are lost, and behavioral advantages are not uniform across scales. Nevertheless, the gains in independent validation and characterization of failure conditions outweigh these losses.
